title: Java port of metriko quad-layout pipeline (Bommes/Campen/Lyon)
description:
**Replaces the entire MSC-based decomposition stack.** After PATCH-22 through PATCH-36, the MSC + Coons-reconstruction pipeline still produces chaotic visual output on the skull (cells with up to 19 sides, Coons spikes, watertight gaps). The architectural problem is structural: MSC tries to derive 4-sided cells from a scalar field's topology, but real meshes don't oblige. The mesh-research consensus (Bommes 2009/2013, Campen 2015, Lyon 2019/2021) is to derive quad cells from a CROSS FIELD (4-direction field with rotational symmetry) plus a SEAMLESS PARAMETRIZATION quantized to integer-grid coordinates. By construction, every cell is exactly 4-sided.

**Reference implementation: komietty/metriko on GitHub** — header-only C++, ~5500 LOC, MPL-2.0. Has all 6 stages (cross field, IGM, motorcycle graph, T-mesh, quantization, QEx) plus a WIP file 'quantization_relinearization.h' that's the Lyon 2021 reparameterization scheme partway done.

**Why port instead of subprocess:** (a) Ixdar targets TeaVM browser builds; can't shell to native binaries. (b) Iteration speed — owning the pipeline means we can tune for our use case. (c) metriko's boundary-mesh limitation needs to be addressed for the skull anyway.

**Pipeline stages (each a sub-ticket as work proceeds):**

1. Linear-algebra foundation. Sparse matrix + Cholesky/LU solver. Baseline: pure Java port of the Eigen subset metriko uses (sparse + dense, real + complex). Could leverage Apache Commons Math3 (already a dep) for some pieces; sparse cholesky may need a custom port. Rough scope: 800-1200 LOC.

2. Cross field. Knöppel-Crane-Pinkall-Schröder smoothest direction field with rotational symmetry. Reference: metriko/include/metriko/core/vectorfield/ (~390 LOC C++). Outputs a 4-RoSy field per face. Scope: 600-900 LOC Java.

3. Seamless parametrization via Integer-Grid Maps (Bommes 2013). Iterative rounding to make UVs integer at singularities. Reference: metriko/include/metriko/core/igm/ (~860 LOC C++). Scope: 1200-1800 LOC Java.

4. Motorcycle-graph T-mesh (Eppstein 2008 / Campen 2015). Trace iso-lines until intersection, build cell decomposition. Reference: metriko/include/metriko/core/tmesh/ (~604 LOC). Scope: 800-1200 LOC.

5. Quantization (Campen 2015). ILP to assign integer arc lengths. Needs an ILP solver in Java — investigate ojAlgo, choco-solver, or our own simplex+branch-and-bound. Reference: metriko/include/metriko/core/quantization/ (~777 LOC). Scope: 1000-1500 LOC + ILP-solver dep.

6. Quad mesh extraction (QEx, Ebke 2013). From a locally-injective UV map, extract the quad faces. Reference: metriko/include/metriko/core/qex/ (~550 LOC). Scope: 700-1000 LOC.

7. Lyon 2021 reparameterization (the WIP piece). Constrained T-mesh quantization with bounded angular separatrix deviation. Reference: metriko's wip/quantization_relinearization.h (361 LOC, marked 'back up') + the Lyon 2021 paper. Scope: 500-800 LOC. Could optionally contribute back to upstream metriko.

8. Boundary support. Skull has openings (foramen magnum, eye sockets, nasal cavity, mandible). metriko's README says 'Meshes with boundaries are currently not supported (planned).' Two approaches: (a) cap the holes pre-processing then re-cut post, (b) extend the algorithm per Lyon 2019 'Parametrization quantization with free boundaries'. Scope: TBD; depends on (a) vs (b).

**Total scope: ~10-15k LOC Java + dependencies.** Multi-month effort; this is a real foundational rewrite.

**References:**
- Lyon, Campen, Kobbelt 2021. Quad Layouts via Constrained T-Mesh Quantization. CGF 40(2). https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/cgf.142634
- Campen 2014 PhD thesis: Quad Layouts — Generation and Optimization of Conforming Quadrilateral Surface Partitions. https://scispace.com/pdf/quad-layouts-generation-and-optimization-of-conforming-1b7xbct85i.pdf
- Campen, Bommes, Kobbelt 2015. Quantized Global Parametrization. SIGGRAPH Asia. https://www.graphics.rwth-aachen.de/media/papers/campen_sa2015_qgp_medium.pdf
- Bommes, Zimmer, Kobbelt 2009. Mixed-integer Quadrangulation. SIGGRAPH 2009.
- Bommes, Campen, Ebke, Alliez, Kobbelt 2013. Integer-Grid Maps for Reliable Quad Meshing. SIGGRAPH 2013.
- Ebke, Bommes, Campen, Kobbelt 2013. QEx: Robust Quad Mesh Extraction. ACM ToG 32(6).
- Knöppel, Crane, Pinkall, Schröder 2013. Globally Optimal Direction Fields. ACM ToG 32.
- Eppstein, Goodrich, Kim, Tamstorf 2008. Motorcycle Graphs: Canonical Quad Mesh Partitioning. CGF 27(5).
- Lyon, Campen, Bommes, Kobbelt 2019. Parametrization quantization with free boundaries for trimmed quad meshing. ACM ToG 38(4).
- komietty/metriko reference implementation: https://github.com/komietty/metriko

**Sub-ticket numbering correction (2026-04-27):** the original description references sub-tickets PATCH-37a through PATCH-37h. Tickets are numbered, not lettered. The actual sub-ticket numbers are PATCH-38 through PATCH-45 in the same order: PATCH-38 = linear algebra foundation (BLOCKER); PATCH-39 = cross field (KCPS); PATCH-40 = Integer-Grid Maps; PATCH-41 = motorcycle T-mesh; PATCH-42 = quantization ILP; PATCH-43 = QEx; PATCH-44 = Lyon 2021 reparameterization; PATCH-45 = boundary support. Linear-algebra dep stack confirmed by ojAlgo survey: ojAlgo (sparse LU, ILP, complex storage) + MTJ ArpackSym (shift-invert Lanczos for KCPS generalized eigenproblem). Both pure Java. See ixdar-tickets/PATCH-37-FILE-PLAN.md for the full file layout.
definition-of-done: 1. Java QgpDecomposer class produces a quad mesh from any input ArrayMesh. 2. Every output cell is exactly 4-sided (validated on cube, sphere, skull). 3. Coons reconstruction watertight (zero gaps) on the skull. 4. Skull-with-boundaries handled either via hole-capping pre-pass or boundary-aware quantization. 5. End-to-end runs on Skull.obj (497k verts) in under 60s. 6. Integration replaces MorseSmaleDecomposer's role in the live viewer + verifier.
testing-plan: 1. Unit tests per stage: cross-field smoothness on a flat plane, IGM injectivity on a sphere, motorcycle-graph cell count on the cube, ILP feasibility on a torus. 2. End-to-end VerifyQgp CLI on cube (expect 6 quads), sphere (expect ~24-48 quads depending on alpha), skull (expect ~hundreds of clean quads). 3. Reuse VerifyCubeReconstruction + VerifySphereReconstruction watertight checks (already in ixdar.cli). 4. Compare visual reconstruction to the reference Polyscope output from metriko on the same input. 5. Measure timing per stage to confirm 60s budget on Skull.obj.\n\n**Sub-tickets to file as work proceeds:** PATCH-37a Linear algebra foundation, PATCH-37b Cross field, PATCH-37c IGM, PATCH-37d Motorcycle T-mesh, PATCH-37e Quantization ILP, PATCH-37f QEx extraction, PATCH-37g Lyon 2021 piece, PATCH-37h Boundary support.
